title: Clean a supplier's SKU list, whichever list the parser built

blocks.text: The catalog importer reads each supplier's feed with one of several parsers and passes the parsed SKU list to `SkuCleaner.clean`. The cleaner passed its tests, and in production it fails for some suppliers and not others; for one supplier the importer's own list came back rewritten.

Write `clean` in `src/main/java/practice/SkuCleaner.java`. It returns the SKUs trimmed, upper-cased, without blank entries or duplicates, in sorted order. Whatever kind of `List` a parser produced, the call must work, and the importer's list must be as it was afterwards. About five lines in total.

cases.says: a feed held in an ArrayList comes back trimmed, upper-cased, without blanks or duplicates, sorted
a feed held in an unmodifiable list is cleaned too, without an exception
the list the importer passed in, even a modifiable one, is unchanged after the call
a feed held in a fixed-size list, which allows set but not remove, is cleaned too

origin.section: List's Mutators Are Optional Operations, So the Caller That Changes Its Argument Is in Breach

concepts: List's mutators are optional operations, so an unmodifiable or fixed-size list keeps the contract by throwing, and a method that changes the list it was given is the code in breach; it builds a new list instead.
